title: EvidenceRecord
description: One row in the frozen evidence ledger. Records are stored per source; the verifier reads them and does not synthesize new ones. There is no merged 'truth graph'.

evidence_id.description: Stable id inside this ledger. Format: `<source>:<record_hash>` — record_hash is SHA-256 of the canonicalized source row, first 16 hex chars.

source.description: Which frozen source this record came from. Must match a manifest under data/manifests/.

snapshot_hash.description: SHA-256 of the raw source file this record was extracted from. Must equal the corresponding manifest's sha256.

record_type.description: What kind of evidence this row is. Governs which claim relations it can license — see spec/inference_rules.md §Evidence licensing.

observation_type.description: `interventional` means the source applied a perturbation and measured the change; `observational` means an association was measured without intervention. Only `interventional` records can license a `causes` claim.

effect.description: Direction and magnitude of the measured effect. Required for record_type=`perturbation_effect` or `expression_observation`; omitted for interaction / annotation records.

magnitude.description: Effect size on the source's native scale (log2FC, correlation coefficient, etc.). Interpretation depends on `magnitude_scale`.

magnitude_scale.description: Free-text tag for the scale (`log2fc`, `pearson_r`, `odds_ratio`). Rules that compare magnitudes must be gated on scale equality.

significance.description: Adjusted p-value or FDR as reported by the source. `null` if the source did not compute one.

contradicts.description: Evidence ids this record directly contradicts under the same context. The verifier uses this to satisfy the CONTRADICTED rule without re-inferring conflicts.

license.description: Free-text license tag from the source's manifest. Records whose license disallows redistribution stay under data/evidence_records/restricted/ and never appear in a published derivation.

source_citation.description: Human-readable citation for the primary study, if the source is a curated aggregator. Rendered in the accepted-claim explanation; never used for identity.
